LESSON: SELECTIVE LISTENING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Selective Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Selective Listening, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to pick out specific details during an oral presentation? 2. Why do we give instructions and directions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. filter required information from an oral text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. take notes from an oral text or recordings on diverse topics,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. give and follow instructions for carrying out different tasks,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. ask for and give directions give clear directions to a place for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. argue for the need to listen attentively to extract specific details. ● in pairs, learners brainstorm ways of selecting and noting down specific information from a listening text, ● in groups, learners are guided to give simple, clear effective instructions to complete tasks and activities, ● in groups, learners are guided to play games such as cue games to enhance selective listening, ● in pairs, learners are guided to simulate, or role play instructions on safety of vehicles during travel, ● in group, learners are guided to share with peers 1. Why is it important to pick out specific details during an oral presentation? 2. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Selective Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● communication and collaboration: the learner’s ability to listen keenly is enhanced as they listen to an audio on

instructions and directions and paraphrases the content.

● digital literacy- using digital technology: the learner sharpens digital skills by recording themselves as they give

instructions and directions in a dialogue.

Values:
Respect: The learner observes etiquette as they play games such as cue games to enhance selective listening.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Socio-economic issues – safety and security: The learner increases their knowledge by listening to a text on travel.

42

● Child road safety – The learner shares with peers how to use emergency exits or operate the door locks of a vehicle,

especially during an accident.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print texts

● braille texts

● Electronic reading materials

● Digital devices with assistive technology

● Audio visual clips

Suggested Skills:

● Taking notes from an oral text or recordings on diverse topics,

● Giving and follow instructions for carrying out different tasks,
